title: 3D Volumetric Method for Quantifying Porosity in Suspended Sediments
author: Lawrence, Carr, et al.

steps.title: Launch ImageJ and Import Data
steps.instruction: Launch ImageJ (v1.52p) and import the image stack data in TIFF format.

substeps.instruction: Select File > Import > Image Sequence

steps.title: Optimize Image Stack
steps.instruction: Process the image stack to reduce noise and isolate floc material.

substeps.instruction: Adjust brightness/contrast (Image > Adjust > Brightness/Contrast) setting min: 6000 and max: 10,000 GL to eliminate high attenuating artefacts and resin block material.
Apply a median 3D filter (Process > Filters > Median 3D) with a radius of 2 × 2 × 2 pixels.
Threshold the image stack (Image > Adjust > Threshold), checking the 'stack histogram' box and setting the threshold value to 16,000 GL.
Rotate the sample block (Image > Transform > Rotate) using the preview slider to an orientation suitable for encapsulation, draw a rectangle around all sample material, and select Image > Crop.
Binarize the dataset (Process > Binary > Make Binary).
Reduce noise by selecting Process > Binary > Erode followed by Process > Binary > Dilate, then save the image stack.

steps.title: Label Floc Samples
steps.instruction: Using ImageJ v1.50e (2015), set the scale and label particles within the binarized stack.

substeps.instruction: Set the scale (Analyze > Set Scale) based on the μCT scan resolution.

Run particle analysis (Plugins > BoneJ > Analyze > Particle Analyser), ticking 'enclosed volume' and 'show particle stack', and setting minimum voxels to 250 voxels/equivalent in μm to screen noise. Retain the results window.

steps.title: Isolate and Identify Sub-sampling Targets
steps.instruction: Segment the labeled flocs and identify specific targets for sub-sampling.

substeps.instruction: Convert the labeled image stack to 8-bit (Image > Type > 8-bit) and run simple segmentation (Plugins > 3D > 3D Simple Segmentation).
Set the scale (Analyze > Set Scale) and open the 3D manager (Plugins > 3D > 3D Manager).
Click 'add image' to load each labeled floc as a separate image. In 3D Manager Options, tick 'Feret (unit)', 'Volume (unit)', and 'Centroid (unit)', then click 'Measure (3D)'.
Combine the Particle Analyser and 3D manager results in spreadsheet software (e.g., MS Excel), ordering by the volume column and matching data by centroid values to select flocs for sub-sampling.

steps.title: Crop Individual Flocs
steps.instruction: Extract individual flocs from the labeled stack into separate files.

substeps.instruction: Reopen the labeled floc stack from step 10, scroll to the end, and open thresholding (Image > Adjust > Threshold).
Enter the specific floc ID number in both value boxes, click 'set', then 'apply' to isolate the selected floc.
Use the Crop 3D plugin (Plugins > Stacks > Crop 3D) to narrow the selection to the floc material plus a small surrounding empty region using x, y, and z plane tools. Save the image stack.

steps.title: Segment Porosity in Individual Flocs
steps.instruction: Using ImageJ v1.52, segment the floc into solid material, total pore space, effective pore space, and isolated pore space.

substeps.instruction: Open the binary volume of the floc (File > Import > Image Sequence).
Apply a closing ball filter (Plugins > MorphoLibJ > Morphological Filters (3D)) with operation 'closing', element shape 'ball', and x/y/z radius of 4/4/4 (~10 μm). Save the output.

Open the original cropped floc (File > Import > Image Sequence) and use Process > Image Calculator to subtract the binary stack from the closing ball output (Image1 = closing ball result, Image2 = binary stack). Save this as the total pore space.
Open the cropped floc again, select Process > Binary > Fill Holes, save, and reopen. Invert the LUT (Image > Lookup Tables > Invert LUT) and save as an inverted fill holes stack.

Merge the total pore space stack (C1) and the inverted fill holes stack (C2) using Image > Colour > Merge Channels (untick 'create composite', tick 'keep source images' and 'ignore source LUTs'). Convert the result to 8-bit (Image > Type > 8-bit).

Use Process > Image Calculator to subtract the merged output (Image2) from the closing ball output (Image1). Save the resulting output containing the 4 phases: solid floc material, total pore space, effective pore space, and isolated pore space.

steps.title: Quantify Bulk Porosity
steps.instruction: Calculate the volume fractions of the different floc phases.

substeps.instruction: Open the closing ball output (stage 17) and the 4-phase segmented output (stage 23).
Use Plugins > BoneJ > Fraction > Volume Fraction to calculate the volume in μm[3] for: overall floc space, isolated pores, effective pores, and solid floc.
Transfer results to a spreadsheet to calculate percentages (total, effective, and isolated porosity) as fractions of the total floc space.

steps.title: Quantify Pore Space Morphology
steps.instruction: Analyze the diameter, shape, tortuosity, and connectivity of the pore volumes.

substeps.instruction: For each segmented volume (total, effective, and isolated pores), open the image stack and run Plugins > BoneJ > Analyze > Particle Analyser, ticking 'Thickness', 'Ellipsoids', and 'Enclosed Volume' to obtain pore diameter, shape, and volume.
Open the volume again and run Plugins > Skeleton > Skeletonize (2D/3D). Save the skeletonized stack.
Run Analyze > Skeleton > Analyze Skeleton (2D/3D) on the skeletonized stack, selecting 'lowest intensity voxel' for Prune cycle method and ticking 'prune ends' and 'show detailed info'.
Use the resulting Euclidean and total running distances to calculate tortuosity, and the number of junctions/nodes and branches to calculate connectivity.
